limitations: Calibration rests on 6 speakers and validation on 3 speakers (one evaluation fold). The 95% speaker-bootstrap interval for the EER is 0.0%–6.4% and for Cllr 0.04–0.20; the point estimates should not be quoted without them.

All validation same-speaker trials come from one session and one channel per speaker. The validation therefore does not cover the within-speaker variability of casework (different sessions, handsets, days, health, speaking style), and same-speaker LRs obtained here are expected to be too high for cross-session pairs; the only cross-session same-speaker pair in the corpus (call 4 ch00 vs call 5 ch00) is the --demo case.

Band-limiting to the telephone band and 10 dB white noise were tested with the clean-trained system applied to degraded evaluation audio (see validation.robustness); other channels, codecs and noise types are untested.

The speaker encoders were trained on Mandarin corpora (3D-Speaker, CN-Celeb) and used zero-shot on Assamese; no Assamese speaker data was used to train them. Language, dialect, gender and age effects are unmeasured: the corpus has no speaker metadata.

The system was chosen post hoc among 40 configurations on the evaluation folds themselves (min mean-of-folds Cllr over the 24 merged 10 s configurations with both folds available (post hoc)), so its own validation figures are optimistically biased.

LRs outside the validated range (log10 LR -0.7 to 2.9 for same-speaker and -4.0 to 1.6 for different-speaker validation trials) are extrapolations of the logistic calibrator and have no empirical support.

The trained backends (LDA, PLDA) were worse than cosine on this corpus because 3–6 training speakers cannot estimate a speaker subspace; the shipped backend is cosine. The remedy is a many-speaker Assamese corpus (IndicVoices, LDC-IL), not a different model.
No automatic check for recording tampering, overlapping speakers, or non-speech content is performed; the energy VAD is not a speech detector and will pass music or noise bursts.
